when: your team leads in kills but has taken no tower and no dragon
asks: we're up in kills what now
we have a bunch of kills how do we use them
we're winning fights but nothing's happening
how do we turn kills into a lead
say: Spend the next kill on a tower or the dragon straight away, or recall and buy first if the gold is still sitting in your pocket.
more: Kills are only gold. They become a lead when they turn into items, a tower or a dragon the other team can't get back.
Each tower you take opens their jungle for the next ten minutes, so later objectives start from your side of the river.
If you chase a second kill instead, they respawn onto waves at your towers and the lead is mostly gone.
check: Which objective is alive, where the side waves are, and how long the dead enemies have left.
breaks: Wrong if nothing is reachable before they respawn: reset together and buy, then set up the next spawn with full items.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: two or more enemies died in the last 20 seconds and your team has more players alive
asks: we won the fight what do we take
they're dead what now
fight's won, tower or dragon
we just killed three what do we do
say: Take the nearest tower with the wave now, or the dragon if it's up and their jungler is one of the dead.
more: A tower is permanent and can't be stolen. A dragon can, so it's the better pick only when their Smite is off the map.
Send one person to the side wave that's about to crash on your tower. Losing that wave quietly hands back part of what you won.
Leave before the respawns. A second fight on low health and no ultimates is how a won fight gets returned.
check: Their death timers, which objective is actually alive, and whether a wave is with you at the tower.
breaks: Wrong if your team is low and the wave isn't there: hitting a tower without minions is slow and risky. Reset and take vision for the next spawn.
basis: pro:After a won fight, the waves decide whether you got paid

when: four or five enemies are dead with long respawn timers after 25:00
asks: they're all dead do we end
ace, can we finish
can we end the game right now
everyone's dead, baron or end
say: Go straight down the lane that already has an open inhibitor and end, or take Baron if no wave can reach their base in time.
more: Ending needs minions at the Nexus towers. Look at where your wave is before you look at the timers.
If the wave is far, Baron is the sure thing: it turns this fight into a base siege they have to defend with every wave pushing.
The worst result is walking halfway, turning around, and getting neither.
check: Where your nearest minion wave is, which of their inhibitors are down, and the shortest enemy death timer.
breaks: Wrong if their first respawn has wave clear and your minions are still at the river: take Baron and the inhibitor instead of racing.
basis: written

when: your team is ahead and you are holding enough gold for a finished item
asks: should i back or keep pushing
i've got a ton of gold do i recall
we're ahead do i need to buy
can i stay out with all this gold
say: Recall and finish the item before the next objective fight, or stay only for a tower that falls in the next few seconds.
more: Gold you carry does nothing in a fight. The real gap between the teams is finished items, and that can be far smaller than the scoreboard looks.
Buying before the spawn means you walk to the pit stronger than they expect. Buying after means you fought it on old items.
Push the wave out first so nothing is lost while you shop.
check: Your gold, how long until the next objective, and whether your wave will hold while you're in base.
breaks: Wrong if an objective starts in under half a minute and your team is already there: stay, fight it, and buy right after.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your team is clearly ahead in kills and towers
asks: should i chase him
can i dive for the kill
he's low do i go in
one more kill, do i go deep
say: Let him go and hold your wave and vision, or take the kill only if he's alone and your ultimates are up.
more: When you're ahead you don't need the kill. They need you to make exactly this kind of deep chase.
A death here gives them a shutdown and an opening at the next objective. Staying alive keeps every later fight in your favour.
The strong version of patience is vision in their jungle: they have to walk into you to get anything.
check: Who is missing on their side, whether your team's big ultimates are back, and whether there's a ward past where he's running.
breaks: Wrong if you can see all five of them and he has no escape left: then it's a free kill, take it and leave.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: your team is ahead, it is past 20:00 and their jungler is alive
asks: do we do baron
we're ahead should we start baron
can we just rush baron
baron now or wait
say: Start Baron to pull them through the dark, then turn and fight, or finish it only once their jungler is dead or shown far away.
more: With a lead, the one thing that can go wrong is a Smite steal. Don't turn a winning game into a fifty-fifty.
Hitting it forces them to walk in through your wards. The fight in that choke is usually better for you than the buff itself.
If nobody comes, you'll see them on a side lane, and that's your cue to finish.
check: Whether the entrances to the pit are warded, where their jungler was last seen, and who on your team is standing alone.
breaks: Wrong if your team can't kill it fast or has no wards around the pit: push the side waves first and come back to it.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize

when: your team killed Baron in the last minute
asks: we got baron what now
how do we use baron
we have baron where do we push
baron buff, group or split
say: Recall, buy, then push two lanes at once so they can't hold both, or go five down one lane if they out-range you.
more: The buff's value is in the minions. Stand with a wave and let the empowered minions hit the tower while you guard them.
Pressure in two lanes splits their wave clear. One lane cracks, and that open inhibitor is what makes the next objective easy.
Don't dive for it. If they clear the wave, back off and wait for the next one.
check: Your gold before you leave base, where each wave is, and which of their towers is closest to falling.
breaks: Wrong if the buff is nearly gone and you're all in base: skip the split and take the one tower you can reach together.
basis: pro:A lead is not power until it is spent

when: your team has three dragons and the next one spawns within a minute
asks: soul point how do we set up
next dragon is soul what do we do
how do we make sure we get soul
we're on three drakes
say: Push mid and the side wave, then walk to the pit together early, or start Baron first if it's up and they camp the dragon.
more: They have to fight this one, so they'll come. Being there first with wards means they walk into you rather than the other way round.
A second objective makes them choose. If they answer Baron, the dragon is free; if they hold dragon, Baron is.
With soul point already banked there's no reason to gamble. If the setup goes badly, back off and try again when the waves are right.
check: Whether your waves are pushed, who has recalled, and whether Baron is available yet.
breaks: Wrong if someone on your team is dead or in base at the spawn: don't start it short-handed, hold the river and wait for five.
basis: pro:A second objective moves the fight

when: your team is ahead and their carries are scaling champions with fewer items than yours
asks: they outscale us how do we close
we're ahead but they scale
how do we beat a late game team
do we need to end fast
say: Take every dragon on spawn so they must fight before their items, or trade it for a tower if they show five at the pit.
more: A scaling team wants a quiet game. Dragons are the clock that stops them waiting, because soul forces a fight on your schedule.
Kills alone are a thin lead against them. Stacked dragons and broken outer towers are what still matter at thirty minutes.
Set the wave and the wards before each spawn so the fight happens while you're still the stronger side.
check: The dragon count for each team, the next spawn time, and how many finished items their carries have.
breaks: Wrong if their carries have already caught up on items: stop forcing, and play for picks and vision instead of front-to-back fights.
basis: pro:Early dragons are the clock against a scaling team

when: your team is ahead and no kills have happened for several minutes
asks: they won't fight us what do we do
they're just sitting under tower
how do we break them when they turtle
nothing's happening and we're ahead
say: Take their jungle camps and ward it so they starve, or push a side lane to pull one of them off the tower.
more: A team that won't leave its towers still needs gold. Their camps are the gold they were counting on.
Wards in their jungle mean the next objective is yours before it spawns, because they can't walk to it unseen.
Diving a full team under a tower is the one way to give the lead back, so make them come out instead.
check: Which of their outer towers are still up, where the side waves are, and whether you have wards to place.
breaks: Wrong if they have strong picks from the fog and you're walking in alone: go in pairs, or stay on the side waves.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: your lane's enemy outer tower has just fallen
asks: we took the tower what now
first tower's down where do i go
do i stay in this lane after tower
tower's gone do we rotate
say: Move to the lane beside the next objective and take that tower too, or stay and farm the long lane if you're the weaker laner.
more: Once the tower is gone the lane is long and dangerous to push. The gold has moved to the other towers.
The tower closest to the next dragon or Baron is the one that matters, because it opens the way to the pit.
Whoever is weakest alone should take the safest lane. The strong duelist takes the long one.
check: Which objective spawns next, which enemy towers are still up, and where their jungler was last seen.
breaks: Wrong if your own tower in that lane is about to fall to the wave: clear it first, then move.
basis: pro:Outer towers are vision

when: you have more kills and items than anyone in the game but your team is not ahead
asks: i'm fed but my team is losing
i'm the only one ahead what do i do
how do i carry this
i'm strong but we're behind
say: Stay near your team and fight at the next objective, where your lead counts, or push one side wave only while you can see their team.
more: Your items win a five on five. They don't win a one on three, and a shutdown on you is their fastest way back.
Being present at dragon or Baron is how one strong player lifts four weaker ones.
Between objectives, take the farm your team can't use safely so the gap on you keeps growing.
check: How many enemies are visible before you step forward, and which teammate can actually follow you.
breaks: Wrong if your team keeps dying before you arrive: then take towers on the far side while the enemy is busy with them.
basis: written

when: an enemy inhibitor has fallen and your team is ahead
asks: inhib's down what now
we got an inhibitor, do we keep going
do we push for the end
inhibitor down, baron or second inhib
say: Back off and take Baron or dragon while the big minions hold that lane, or open a second inhibitor if they send two to clear.
more: An open inhibitor pins someone in their base every wave. That's a player missing from the next objective fight.
Use that time on Baron or the soul dragon instead of diving Nexus towers with everyone alive.
Two open lanes is usually the end: they can't clear both and still walk out.
check: Which objectives are alive, how many enemies are clearing the pushed lane, and your team's health.
breaks: Wrong if they're already dead or split: then keep going with the wave and finish it.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: you are ahead of their bot laner in items and kills
asks: i'm a fed adc how do i close
i'm ahead as adc what do i do
where should i be as the carry
i'm strong, do i go side lane
say: Stay mid with your support and hit towers with the wave, or take a side wave only when you can see four of them.
more: You're the tower damage. The team's lead turns into buildings fastest when you're alive at the front of a wave.
A carry caught alone on a side lane is the classic way a lead gets thrown, because you can't escape most picks.
Mid is the short lane. It's the safest place to farm and the closest to both pits.
check: Where their assassins and engage champions are before you step past the river.
breaks: Wrong if someone on your team with an escape can't hold the side lane and waves are crashing: go with your support, clear it, and come straight back.
basis: written

when: you are ahead and an objective spawns in about a minute
asks: i'm fed as assassin what now
do i look for picks or group
how do i use my lead as an assassin
who do i go for
say: Wait in the fog on their path to the pit and catch whoever walks first, or stay beside your team if their carries move together.
more: A kill just before the spawn makes the objective a four on five. That's worth more than the same kill two minutes earlier.
Your lead fades as they buy defensive items and stop walking alone, so use it on objectives now.
If they're grouped, wait for the fight to start and go in second, on whoever used their escape.
check: Whether the brush you want to sit in is warded, and who on their team still has Flash.
breaks: Wrong if they have a ward on you and all five show together: don't go in first, fight with your team at the pit.
basis: pro:Time the pick against the objective clock

when: you are ahead of their side laner and Baron is available
asks: do i split or group
i'm ahead in side lane, baron's up
should i keep pushing side
do i tp to baron or push
say: Push the lane opposite Baron so they must send two, or walk to your team early if you have no Teleport to join.
more: If two come to stop you, your team has four against three at the pit. If one comes and loses, you take the inhibitor.
The push only works if your team knows not to fight until they answer you.
Without Teleport you can't join a fight that starts, so the pressure has to end before the spawn.
check: How many enemies show in your lane, whether your Teleport is up, and whether your team is waiting rather than fighting.
breaks: Wrong if your team starts the fight four on five without you: next time group, because this team won't hold.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: your team is ahead and an objective spawns in about a minute
asks: where do i ward when we're ahead
we're winning what do i do as support
do i go deep for vision
should i ward their jungle
say: Ward the entrances from their jungle to the pit with someone beside you, or stay on your carry if nobody will come.
more: When you're ahead, vision goes forward. Seeing them leave base tells your team when to start and when to turn.
Go a minute early. Wards placed as the objective spawns are placed into their whole team.
A support caught alone before the spawn hands them the objective, so the escort matters more than one extra ward.
check: Who is walking with you, how many enemies are visible, and whether you have wards and a sweeper ready.
breaks: Wrong if three or more of them are missing: ward the river on your side only and wait for your team.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: your team is ahead and you are the engage champion
asks: when do i engage if we're ahead
do i just go in
we're ahead should i start fights
who do i engage on
say: Engage only when an objective is up to take afterwards, or stand in front and make them start the fight instead.
more: A fight with nothing to take after it is a risk without a prize. Tie your engage to a dragon, Baron or tower.
Ahead, your team's damage wins a slow front-to-back fight. You don't need a perfect flank.
Holding your engage also holds their carries back, which is how a siege gets free tower damage.
check: Whether your damage dealers are close enough to follow, and which enemy escapes you've seen used.
breaks: Wrong if one of them walks up alone in front of their tower: that's a free start, take it.
basis: pro:Cooldowns spent before the objective decide it

when: the Elder dragon is spawning and your team is ahead
asks: elder is up we're ahead
do we need elder
elder or baron when ahead
how do we set up elder
say: Push all three waves and take Elder as five, or use Baron on the other side to drag them off it first.
more: Elder is the one buff that can lose you a winning game, so denying it matters as much as getting it.
With waves pushing, they lose towers for standing at the pit. That's the pressure that makes them walk in badly.
Their jungler is the only threat. Zone him, don't race him.
check: Where the three waves are, whether the pit entrances are warded, and where their jungler stands.
breaks: Wrong if a carry of yours is dead or in base: don't start it, just hold the area until they're back.
basis: pro:Push the side waves before you posture at Baron

when: their jungler is dead and an objective is alive
asks: their jungler died what do i do as laner
jungler's dead do i leave lane
should i help with dragon
enemy jungle is dead what's free
say: Shove your wave and walk to the objective now, it can't be stolen, or stay for plates if your team already has enough there.
more: With no Smite against you, the take is safe as long as enough bodies arrive to finish it before he respawns.
Pushing first means your tower isn't losing minions while you're gone, and their laner is late to follow.
If three teammates are already on it, your plates are extra gold on top.
check: His respawn timer, how many teammates are already at the pit, and where your wave is.
breaks: Wrong if your wave is under your own tower and big: you lose more staying away than you add at the pit.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: your team killed the grubs or the Herald
asks: we got grubs how do we use them
we have herald where do we use it
what do grubs do for us
herald mid or side
say: Use it on the tower nearest the next dragon just before it spawns, or on the lane where your strongest laner already has plates.
more: Both are tower-taking tools. They're wasted if nobody hits towers in the next few minutes.
A tower threatened in mid right before a dragon makes them answer two places. Whichever they pick, you get the other.
Stacking it onto a winning lane is the simple version: one early tower, then that laner moves.
check: Who is holding the Herald, when the next dragon spawns, and which enemy tower is lowest.
breaks: Wrong if their team can kill the Herald before it reaches the tower: wait for a bigger wave to carry it in.
basis: pro:Herald in mid before a dragon buys the river

when: your team is ahead and one of your teammates has died twice in the last few minutes
asks: we keep giving kills while ahead
how do we stop throwing
we're ahead but people keep dying
are we throwing
say: Stop taking fights away from objectives and group for the next spawn, or mirror their side laner if you're the one who can duel.
more: Leads get thrown one pick at a time, usually on someone farming alone past the river with no ward.
Each death is a shutdown plus a numbers gap at the next objective. Two in a row and the game is even.
Grouping early costs a few minions and removes the picks they need.
check: Who on your team is alone past the river, and how long until the next objective.
breaks: Wrong if the deaths are coming in forced fights at objectives rather than picks: then the issue is setup, so arrive earlier with wards.
basis: pro:When ahead, let them come to you

when: your team is behind in kills before 14:00
asks: we're losing early what do i do
bad start how do we come back
we're behind already
everyone's losing lane what now
say: Farm every wave you can reach safely and give the contested objective, or join a fight only when you arrive with equal numbers.
more: An early deficit is a few kills of gold. It shrinks every minute you farm evenly and grows every time you fight a level down.
A given dragon is cheaper than a lost fight for it, as long as it isn't their soul point.
The comeback usually comes later, at one objective where they overreach and you arrive together.
check: Your wave position, who on your team is close enough to help, and where their jungler last showed.
breaks: Wrong if they're diving you under tower every wave: ask for help or give the tower and farm further back.
basis: pro:Do not fight an objective one spike behind

when: your team is behind in kills and towers
asks: we're behind how do we come back
how do we win from behind
what do we do when losing
we're losing mid game what's the plan
say: Catch waves near your towers and stay within reach of each other, or collapse together when one of them walks too far in.
more: The team ahead has to come to you to end. That walk through your jungle is where they get caught.
Farming under your towers closes the item gap for free. Fighting in the river on their vision widens it.
One good pick before an objective can flip it, so keep your ultimates for that moment.
check: Which waves are safe to reach, where their strongest player is, and whether your key ultimates are up.
breaks: Wrong if they never overextend and keep taking objectives: you'll have to pick one, most likely the soul-point dragon, and fight it together.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: you have more deaths than kills and fewer items than your lane opponent
asks: i'm behind what do i do
i'm useless how do i help
i fed, how do i play now
i'm way down in my lane
say: Take the safest wave and the camps nobody is using, or stick to your strongest teammate and use your crowd control for them.
more: Behind, your damage is unreliable but your abilities still work. A stun or a slow for the fed ally is real value.
Safe farm is slower but it's the only gold that doesn't risk another shutdown for them.
A cheaper defensive item often does more than chasing your damage build.
check: Which wave is closest to your tower, who your strongest teammate is, and your gold.
breaks: Wrong if your team needs your damage and nobody else has it: then farm until one item, and only then join fights.
basis: written

when: your team is behind but you have more items than your lane opponent
asks: i'm ahead but my team is losing
team's behind and i'm the only one doing well
can i carry from behind
do i split when team is losing
say: Fight beside your team at the next objective so they can play around you, or take a tower elsewhere if they concede it.
more: You're the reason a fight can still be won. If you're across the map, the other four can't contest anything.
Their team will look for you first. Stay where a teammate can peel, and let them spend abilities getting to you.
If your team gives the objective, don't hover. Take a tower so something comes back.
check: Whether your team is actually going to the objective, and which enemy is strong enough to duel you.
breaks: Wrong if your team won't group at all: then push the lane furthest from them and take what towers you can.
basis: pro:If you cannot contest, take something elsewhere at once

when: your team is behind and your carries are scaling champions
asks: we scale, how do we survive until then
how do i stall for late game
we just need time what do we do
how long do we need to stall
say: Give the early dragons and keep every wave off your towers, or fight only the dragon that would give them soul.
more: Your team gets stronger each wave, so the plan is to make the game long and lose as few towers as possible.
Dragons before soul point are a price you can pay. The soul itself isn't, so plan recalls and ultimates around that one.
Until then, nobody dies for a ward or a camp.
check: The dragon count for each team, the next spawn time, and how many items your carries have finished.
breaks: Wrong if they're taking towers instead of dragons: then the towers are the clock, so defend those and give the dragons.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: the enemy team has three dragons and the next one spawns within a minute
asks: they're on soul point
do we have to fight this dragon
they have three drakes what do we do
can we give soul
say: Recall now, buy, and get to the pit first as five, or send your jungler in for the steal if they're already on it.
more: Soul is the one dragon you can't trade. Everything you gave earlier was to be ready for this fight.
Being there first lets you fight from your side with wards down. Arriving late means walking into them through a choke.
If it's lost anyway, a steal attempt is worth the jungler's life here in a way it wasn't on dragon one.
check: Who is dead or in base, whose Teleport is up, and whether your jungler has Smite ready.
breaks: Wrong if two of you are dead at the spawn: don't walk in three on five, take a tower or Baron on the other side.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team is behind and an enemy has just died alone
asks: we got a pick what now
we killed one do we fight
one's dead should we go baron
we caught someone, what do we take
say: Take the closest tower or objective right now while it's five on four, or just clear vision and reset if he was their weakest.
more: From behind, a numbers edge is the only time fights are fair. It lasts as long as his respawn timer.
A tower or dragon gets something permanent out of it. Chasing a second kill usually gives the pick back.
Who died matters. Their jungler dead means objectives; their carry dead means you can fight.
check: Who died and for how long, which objective is alive, and where the rest of them are.
breaks: Wrong if the other four are already grouped on you and still stronger: clear the waves and back off.
basis: pro:A dead jungler makes the objective free

when: the enemy team killed Baron in the last minute
asks: they got baron how do we defend
they have baron what do we do
how do we survive baron
baron push coming
say: Clear each wave from behind your towers and don't step out, or engage only if one of them dives past the minions.
more: The buff is in the minions. Kill the wave and the push stops, and every wave you clear runs time off it.
Fighting them in the open with the buff active is what they want. Losing a tower is cheaper than losing a fight.
Use your long-range abilities on minions first, champions second.
check: Which lanes are pushing, who on your team clears waves fastest, and how many enemies show in each lane.
breaks: Wrong if they split and one is alone in a side lane with no escape: collapse on him fast, then return to the towers.
basis: written

when: one enemy has far more kills and items than anyone else
asks: how do we deal with the fed guy
one of them is super fed
who do i focus
do we kill the fed one or avoid him
say: Save your crowd control for him when he comes in, or fight on the side of the map where he isn't.
more: A fed player usually has to step forward to use his lead. That step is when all your stuns land on him at once.
Killing him pays a big shutdown, which is the fastest gold a losing team can get.
If you can't lock him down, the answer is to make plays where he's absent: he can only be in one lane.
check: Where he is on the map, whether his Flash was used, and who on your team has crowd control ready.
breaks: Wrong if he has range and never steps in: don't walk at him, go for whoever is in front of him.
basis: written

when: your team is behind
asks: where do i ward when we're behind
is it safe to ward
do i go for deep vision
where does vision go when losing
say: Ward your own jungle entrances and the river brush nearest your tower, or go further only with your team walking beside you.
more: Behind, vision is for not getting picked. Wards that show them coming into your jungle are worth more than wards on their camps.
It also tells your side laners when it's safe to catch a wave.
Dying for a ward before an objective gives them the objective, so the deep ward is rarely worth it.
check: How many enemies are missing, who is near you, and how many wards you're carrying.
breaks: Wrong if a soul-point dragon or Baron fight is coming and you must contest: then go early, as five, and ward the pit together.
basis: pro:Before a spawn, arrive alive and on time

when: you are behind as an assassin
asks: i'm a behind assassin what do i do
i can't kill anyone
how do i play assassin from behind
i do no damage now
say: Look for whoever pushes a side wave alone and low, or wait in a fight and go in after their key abilities are used.
more: Behind, you can't burst a full-health carry. You can still finish someone who's already been hit.
Side waves are where their team is alone. One pick there before an objective evens the fight.
Going in second also means their peel has already been spent on someone else.
check: The target's health and items, whether he has Flash, and whether his team is near.
breaks: Wrong if they're always grouped: stop hunting, catch waves until an item, and stay near your team's fight.
basis: written

when: your team is behind and you are the engage champion
asks: should i engage when we're behind
do i go in or peel
we're losing do i start fights
how do i play tank from behind
say: Hold your engage to stop whoever dives your carry, or use it forward only on someone caught alone near your tower.
more: A forward engage from behind usually means your team follows into more damage than it has.
Used second, your crowd control turns their dive into a kill for your side. That's the comeback fight.
A lone target near your tower is the exception, because your team arrives first.
check: Where your carry is standing, who on their team dives, and whether your team is close enough to follow.
breaks: Wrong if their carry stands alone in front with no Flash: engage on him, that chance doesn't wait.
basis: written

when: you are behind as the bot lane carry
asks: i'm a behind adc what do i do
i die instantly in fights
how do i play adc when losing
where do i farm when behind
say: Farm mid and the nearest safe side wave until your next item, or in a fight just hit whoever is closest to you.
more: You scale with items, so the fastest comeback is uncontested waves, not fights.
Hitting the front line is fine. Walking past it to reach their carry is how you die first.
Stay behind your tank and on the side of the fight away from their assassin.
check: Where their divers are, how far you are from the item, and whether your support is with you.
breaks: Wrong if your team needs you at a soul-point dragon or Baron: go, because without your damage they can't contest.
basis: written

when: your team is behind and you have long-range wave clear
asks: what's my job when we're behind
how do i help us stall
i'm a mage and we're losing
do i poke or clear waves
say: Kill the wave before it reaches your tower every time, or poke their front line when they stand still at a siege.
more: Without minions they can't hit the tower. Your wave clear is the reason a siege fails.

more: Most leads this size get handed back by one bad dive or a pick before an objective.
Your side gets relatively stronger as items fill out, because their extra gold has less to buy.
Choose the fight in advance, usually soul point or Baron, and have everyone alive and bought for it.
check: The dragon count, the Baron timer, and how many items your strongest player has.
breaks: Wrong if your base is already open: then every wave comes first, and the fight has to happen at your towers.
basis: pro:Give early dragons, then fight the one before soul point

when: your team leads in kills but trails in towers or dragons
asks: we have more kills are we ahead
we're up kills but it feels bad
why are we not winning
kills up, towers down
say: Treat it as even: turn the next kill into a tower or dragon, or stop fighting and match their farm.
more: Kills are gold once. Towers and dragons are map and stats for the rest of the game.
If they have the structures, they also have the safer farm, so the item gap may be smaller than it looks.
Compare finished items on the carries. That's the honest scoreboard.
check: Item counts on both teams' carries, and which objective is next.
breaks: Wrong if your kills are all on one player who's now far ahead: then play around him at the next objective.
basis: pro:Kills are not a lead if the farm went the other way

when: your team trails in kills but leads in towers or dragons
asks: we're down kills are we losing
they have more kills but we have towers
is this even
who's actually ahead
say: You're fine: keep taking objectives and avoid random fights, or fight only at the next dragon with everyone there.
more: Structures and dragons last. Their kill gold only matters if they get to use it in a fight.
They'll look for fights to make the kills count. Not giving them is how your map lead grows.
At an objective you still have to show up as five, because that's where their kills do matter.
check: Dragon count, towers left on each side, and where their most fed player is.
breaks: Wrong if one of them is so far ahead he wins fights alone: then save crowd control for him before anything else.
basis: written

when: no objective is alive and none spawns within a minute
asks: what should i be doing right now
nothing's up what do i do
where should i be
what's the plan right now
say: Catch the furthest wave you can reach safely, then recall before the next spawn, or take camps with your jungler if lanes are covered.
more: Quiet time is farm time. The team that wastes it arrives at the next objective an item short.
Pushing a wave before you leave makes their player catch it, which makes them late.
Plan backwards from the spawn: wave, recall, buy, walk. If you start late, something gets skipped.
check: The next objective timer, your gold, and how many enemies are visible before you go far.
breaks: Wrong if three or more of them are missing: take the wave closer to your tower instead.
basis: pro:The lane that pushes first moves first

when: a dragon was killed in the last minute
asks: when's the next dragon
what's the next objective
what do we play for next
when does drake come back
say: The next dragon is five minutes after that kill, so play for a tower or Baron side until then, or farm and buy for it.
more: Five minutes is enough for two recalls and a tower, so nobody needs to hover the pit.
Whatever is on the top side comes first now: grubs or Herald early, Baron after twenty minutes.
Be bought and walking about a minute before the dragon returns.
check: The game time of the kill, each team's dragon count, and what's alive in the top pit.
breaks: Wrong if that kill gave a team soul: the next one is Elder, and that changes how hard you prepare.
basis: rule

when: the game is even in kills and towers
asks: what's our win condition
how do we win this
what's the plan for this game
who do we play around
say: Play around whichever ally has the most items and fight where they are, or stack dragons if nobody stands out.
more: In an even game, one player ahead is the win condition. Fights near them go better than fights without them.
If nobody is ahead, the win condition is the objective race: dragons toward soul and the first Baron.
Look at their team the same way. Whoever is strongest for them is the one you avoid or lock down.
check: Item counts for each player, and the dragon count.
breaks: Wrong if your strongest player is a split pusher: then the team plays opposite him, not next to him.
basis: written

when: the game is even after 25:00
asks: how do we close this out
how do we win from here
it's even and late, what wins
what ends this game
say: Win the next Baron or Elder and push with it, or catch one of them alone and take that objective for free.
more: Late games end on one objective. Everything before it is setup: waves, vision, everyone alive.
A pick does the same job as winning the fight, with less risk.
After the objective, go for an inhibitor. That's what makes the following one easier still.
check: Which big objective is alive or spawning, and where your waves are.
breaks: Wrong if your team is the one better at long fights at the tower: then make them come to you with waves instead.
basis: pro:Time the pick against the objective clock

when: it is before 14:00 and one of your lanes is ahead in CS and kills while another is behind
asks: which lane do we play for
who's our strong side
should we help the losing lane
where should the team be
say: Play toward the winning lane and take its tower and nearby objective, or cover the losing lane only to stop a dive.
more: Help spent on a lane that's ahead becomes a tower. Help spent on a lane that's far behind often becomes another death.
The losing lane's job is to give nothing more: farm at the tower and skip trades.
The first tower from the strong side then frees that laner to move.
check: Which objective is on the strong lane's side, and whether the weak lane's wave is at its tower.
breaks: Wrong if the losing lane holds your late-game carry: one visit to steady it can be worth more.
basis: pro:The lane without help gives nothing

when: your team is behind and no ally has died for several minutes
asks: are we stabilizing
is the stall working
we stopped dying, now what
are we catching up
say: It's working, so keep farming and line up one objective fight, or keep stalling if your carries are still an item short.
more: No deaths means their lead has stopped growing while your items catch up.
Stalling isn't the win, though. At some point you take a fight, and it should be at a spawn you prepared for.
Decide which one now so recalls and ultimates are ready.
check: Item counts on your carries against theirs, and the next two objective timers.
breaks: Wrong if they're taking towers for free the whole time: then you're not stalling, you're bleeding, and need to contest waves sooner.
basis: written

when: your team is ahead and it is past 20:00
asks: we're ahead why isn't the game ending
how do we actually finish
we've been ahead forever
why can't we close
say: Take Baron off a pick or with their jungler shown elsewhere, then push two lanes, or break an inhibitor before the next dragon.
more: Leads stall when a team keeps winning fights but takes nothing that opens the base.
Baron is the tool for that. Empowered minions crack the towers you can't dive.
One open inhibitor then makes every later objective a fight they start a player short.
check: Whether Baron is alive, where their jungler is, and which of their inner towers is weakest.
breaks: Wrong if their wave clear holds every push: then use vision and picks first, don't siege into it.
basis: pro:With a lead, Baron is bait before it is a prize
